source.paper_title: RUNLTS: Register-value-aware Predictor Utilizing Nested Large Tables

summary: Captures correlations between register values and branch directions by feeding digests of recently produced register values into the statistical corrector (SC). A Tomasulo-like table tracks valid register values, generating a 12-bit digest from integers, floats, or condition-code flags. At prediction time, for each of the 8 banks, the register with the highest usefulness score is chosen, and its digest is used to look up prediction weights which are summed into the overall SC prediction.

state.name: tomasulo_table
state.organization: Flat table with one entry per logical register
state.entry_format: valid (1 bit), payload (14 bits: holds ROB index when valid=0, or 12-bit digest when valid=1), decay_ctr (8 bits)

state.name: ut0
state.entry_format: Vector of num_logical_regs weights, each ut_weight_bits wide

state.name: ut1
state.entry_format: Vector of num_logical_regs weights, each ut_weight_bits wide

state.name: ut2
state.entry_format: Vector of num_logical_regs weights, each ut_weight_bits wide

state.name: wt0
state.organization: Prediction weight table 0, split into num_banks
state.indexing: bank ID and hash0(PC, digest) % wt0_entries

state.name: wt1
state.organization: Prediction weight table 1, split into num_banks
state.indexing: bank ID and hash1(PC, digest) % wt1_entries

state.name: wt2
state.organization: Prediction weight table 2, split into num_banks
state.indexing: bank ID and hash2(PC, digest) % wt2_entries

state.name: inflight_prediction_metadata
state.organization: Queue storing metadata for each in-flight branch to be used at update time
state.entry_format: available_mask (num_logical_regs bits), best_r_per_bank (num_banks * 7 bits), digest_per_bank (num_banks * 12 bits)

algorithms.name: allocate_tomasulo
algorithms.pseudocode:
if instruction_writes_register:
  r = instruction.dest_logical_reg
  tomasulo_table[r].valid = 0
  tomasulo_table[r].payload = instruction.rob_index
algorithms.notes: Invalidates the register's digest and records the producer's ROB index.

algorithms.name: compute_digest
algorithms.notes: UNCERTAIN (U3/U4) resolved by: INT counts modulo 64 and zero/one is not distinguished; FP formats are right-aligned at bit 3.

algorithms.name: update_tomasulo
algorithms.pseudocode:
if instruction_writes_register:
  r = instruction.dest_logical_reg
  rob = instruction.rob_index
  if tomasulo_table[r].valid == 0 and tomasulo_table[r].payload == rob:
    tomasulo_table[r].payload = compute_digest(instruction.value, instruction.type)
    tomasulo_table[r].valid = 1
    tomasulo_table[r].decay_ctr = (decay_threshold - 1) & ((1 << decay_ctr_bits) - 1)
algorithms.notes: Writes the computed digest and sets the valid bit if the entry was waiting for this specific instruction.

algorithms.name: decay_tomasulo
algorithms.notes: Decays the validity of each digest. Triggered per decoded instruction. Threshold is 256.

algorithms.name: recover_tomasulo
algorithms.notes: The paper leaves recovery as future work (Section 5). This is an assumed lightweight rollback that invalidates entries allocated by squashed instructions.

algorithms.name: predict
algorithms.notes: Aggregates the usefulness of registers per bank, picks the most useful, looks up weights with its digest, and adds to sR.

algorithms.name: update
algorithms.pseudocode:
def saturate_add(val, amt, bits):
  max_v = (1 << (bits - 1)) - 1
  return max_v if val + amt > max_v else val + amt

def saturate_sub(val, amt, bits):
  min_v = -(1 << (bits - 1))
  return min_v if val - amt < min_v else val - amt

def was_bank_useful(b, outcome):
  return host_was_bank_useful(b, outcome)

outcome = host_commit_outcome(branch_id)
metadata = inflight_prediction_metadata[branch_id % num_inflight_branches]
ut_idx0 = hash(PC) % ut0_entries
ut_idx1 = hash(PC) % ut1_entries
ut_idx2 = hash(PC) % ut2_entries

for b in 0 .. num_banks - 1:
  # Update Prediction Tables (WT)
  best_r = metadata.best_r_per_bank[b]
  if best_r != -1 and sc_update_needed:
    digest = metadata.digest_per_bank[b]
    h0 = hash0(PC, digest) % wt0_entries
    h1 = hash1(PC, digest) % wt1_entries
    h2 = hash2(PC, digest) % wt2_entries
    if outcome == TAKEN:
      wt0[b][h0] = saturate_add(wt0[b][h0], 1, wt_weight_bits)
      wt1[b][h1] = saturate_add(wt1[b][h1], 1, wt_weight_bits)
      wt2[b][h2] = saturate_add(wt2[b][h2], 1, wt_weight_bits)
    else:
      wt0[b][h0] = saturate_sub(wt0[b][h0], 1, wt_weight_bits)
      wt1[b][h1] = saturate_sub(wt1[b][h1], 1, wt_weight_bits)
      wt2[b][h2] = saturate_sub(wt2[b][h2], 1, wt_weight_bits)
  
  # Update Usefulness Tables (UT)
  available_in_bank = []
  for r in 0 .. num_logical_regs - 1:
    if (r % num_banks) == b and (metadata.available_mask & (1 << r)):
      available_in_bank = available_in_bank + [r]
  
  if len(available_in_bank) > 0 and sc_update_needed:
    rand_r = random_choice(available_in_bank)
    if was_bank_useful(b, outcome):
      ut0[ut_idx0][rand_r] = saturate_add(ut0[ut_idx0][rand_r], 1, ut_weight_bits)
      ut1[ut_idx1][rand_r] = saturate_add(ut1[ut_idx1][rand_r], 1, ut_weight_bits)
      ut2[ut_idx2][rand_r] = saturate_add(ut2[ut_idx2][rand_r], 1, ut_weight_bits)
    else:
      ut0[ut_idx0][rand_r] = saturate_sub(ut0[ut_idx0][rand_r], 1, ut_weight_bits)
      ut1[ut_idx1][rand_r] = saturate_sub(ut1[ut_idx1][rand_r], 1, ut_weight_bits)
      ut2[ut_idx2][rand_r] = saturate_sub(ut2[ut_idx2][rand_r], 1, ut_weight_bits)
algorithms.notes: Selects a random available register in each bank to update its UT weights. Updates WT weights corresponding to the selected digest.

host_interfaces.need: destination logical register and ROB index at decode
host_interfaces.description: Trigger on instruction decode with destination logical register and ROB index to allocate an entry in the Tomasulo-like table.
host_interfaces.fallback: If unavailable at decode, allocate at dispatch or skip allocating.

host_interfaces.description: Trigger on instruction completion with the produced value, type (INT, FP16, etc.), and ROB index to compute the digest and mark the Tomasulo table entry valid.
host_interfaces.fallback: Extract values directly from the physical register file or completion bus if ROB is not tracked.

host_interfaces.description: Trigger to decay the valid digests in the Tomasulo table per decoded instruction.
host_interfaces.fallback: Decay based on cycles or fetch packets instead of individual decoded instructions.

host_interfaces.description: Trigger to roll back the Tomasulo table allocation for flushed instructions.
host_interfaces.fallback: Clear all valid=0 entries or flush the entire Tomasulo table.

resource_accounting.storage_breakdown: tomasulo_table: 1495 bits; ut0: 3120 bits; ut1: 3120 bits; ut2: 3120 bits; wt0: 24576 bits; wt1: 12288 bits; wt2: 6144 bits; inflight_prediction_metadata: 27776 bits.
resource_accounting.logic_cost_notes: The paper states sR costs 53,863 bits (Table 3). This spec is over budget by 27,776 bits because the paper does not account for the prediction-time metadata (available registers and chosen digests per bank) that must be held until update time. The spec provisions 128 entries for this.
resource_accounting.budget_donors: Large Bimodal predictor or TAGE high banks can be shrunk to pay for the feature.

parameters.name: num_logical_regs
parameters.storage_impact: Linear impact on tomasulo_table, ut0, ut1, ut2, and inflight_prediction_metadata.

parameters.name: num_banks
parameters.storage_impact: Linear impact on wt0, wt1, wt2, and inflight_prediction_metadata.

parameters.name: ut_weight_bits
parameters.storage_impact: Linear factor for ut0, ut1, ut2.

parameters.name: wt_weight_bits
parameters.storage_impact: Linear factor for wt0, wt1, wt2.

parameters.name: decay_threshold
parameters.storage_impact: No direct storage impact, assuming decay_ctr_bits is large enough.

parameters.name: algorithms_1_variant
parameters.question: How should the leading and trailing counts be encoded (e.g., modulo 64, saturate at 63), and how is the zero/one case distinguished?

parameters.name: algorithms_1_variant_2
parameters.question: Are the extracted FP fields right-aligned at digest bit 3 or bit 0, and how is the format classification performed for values that are not recognisable floats?

parameters.name: algorithms_1_pseudocode_variant
parameters.question: How are the three 6-bit fields for INT registers combined into the 12-bit digest?

parameters.name: algorithms_1_pseudocode_variant_2
parameters.question: How does the 6-bit count field encode counts up to 64 for integer registers?

unit_tests.name: decay_counter_expires
unit_tests.given: A register is completed (update_tomasulo) setting its decay_ctr to decay_threshold. decay_tomasulo is triggered decay_threshold times.
unit_tests.expect: The register's decay_ctr reaches 0, which causes its valid bit in tomasulo_table to be set to 0.

unit_tests.name: digest_computation_int
unit_tests.given: update_tomasulo is called for an INT instruction with value 0x...0F, invoking compute_digest.
unit_tests.expect: compute_digest computes the correct folded value and stores it in tomasulo_table.

unit_tests.name: predict_chooses_max_u
unit_tests.given: predict is called with two registers valid in the same bank, having different weight sums in ut0, ut1, ut2.
unit_tests.expect: predict selects the register with the higher usefulness, looks up weights in wt0, wt1, wt2 using its digest, stores choices in inflight_prediction_metadata, and adds the scaled sum to sR.

unit_tests.name: update_modifies_tables
unit_tests.given: update is called after predict has populated inflight_prediction_metadata.
unit_tests.expect: update reads the chosen digest to adjust wt0, wt1, wt2, and randomly selects one available register from the mask to adjust ut0, ut1, ut2.

unit_tests.name: squash_recovery_clears_invalid_rob
unit_tests.given: allocate_tomasulo is called for register R. recover_tomasulo is triggered for an older branch.
unit_tests.expect: tomasulo_table[R].valid becomes 1 and its payload is cleared.

open_questions: Tomasulo recovery: The paper leaves this to future work. Assumed a lightweight invalidation of in-flight allocations based on ROB age.

[/algorithms/2/pseudocode] U4 (part 2): The format-classification step ('we inspect the most significant bits to classify the format') is ambiguous as the mechanism is not specified, nor is the handling of non-float values. The spec assumes the host provides the exact type. Also raised at /algorithms/1/pseudocode.

The paper defines UT entries as 8- or 9-element vectors (one weight per register in the bank), but the spec implements a single 65-element vector. It is unspecified if bank UTs are meant to be independent tables with independent indexing.
Figure 5(c) labels the UT input as 'PC (skewed)' and its output as '9 regs useful (skewed)', but the exact skewing transformation is undefined.
[/unit_tests/4] What is the correct recovery mechanism for the Tomasulo table on a squash?
[/parameters/12/default] What is the maximum number of in-flight branches the predictor metadata must support? Also raised at /parameters/12.
[/parameters/14] The multiplier used when a bank's usefulness is not positive is 0.0. (reviewer cited unverifiable evidence; treat as assumed)

[/algorithms/4/pseudocode] How should the Tomasulo-like table be recovered on a squash? Specifically, what should the valid bit and payload be set to when an allocated instruction is squashed? Also raised at /unit_tests/4.
[/state/7/size_formula] How is the prediction-time register availability and digest metadata stored and passed to the update stage, and what is its budget?
[/parameters/13/default] What is the precise scaling factor for a useful bank?
[/algorithms/6/pseudocode] What is the exact logic for 'was_bank_useful(b, outcome)'? Does it compare the bank's prediction against the final true outcome, or against the base predictor?
[/algorithms/6/pseudocode] The 'outcome' variable is required to update weights but is never produced by any algorithm in the spec. How is the true branch outcome passed to the update stage?

[/algorithms/5/pseudocode] [source U2: Figure 5 (c) Proposed Register Components] the input marks this UNCERTAIN, so it must not be resolved by assumption: The figure does not label the wire that selects x0 vs x2.5. The panel (a)/(b) analogy and the "largest / Most useful in this bank" output make the bank's own usefulness value the natural driver, but this is not drawn explicitly. The alternative reading - a single global static scale of 2.5 - is not consistent with an "x0" option existing at all, but cannot be ruled out from the figure alone.

[source I10: Figure 5 (c) Proposed Register Components] the input marks this INFERRED -- a reading of the figure's layout that the paper never states -- so whatever the spec derives from it is an assumption and not a fact: bank membership. Bank 0's register list "R0, R8, R16, ... R64" is a stride-8 sequence, i.e. bank i holds the logical registers r with r mod 8 == i. Bank 0 therefore holds 9 registers (R0..R64) and banks 1..7 hold 8 each, totalling 65 - matching the "eight or nine logical registers" of Section 4.2, the "9x6bit" UT entry annotation, and the factor 65 in Table 3.

[/unit_tests/0] Reviewers disagreed on /unit_tests/0: The decay counter expires after a symbolic decay_threshold. | The decay_counter_expires test verifies a 256-step countdown using an 8-bit counter. | The digest is invalidated when decay_tomasulo is triggered a variable 'decay_threshold' times.

[/parameters/10] The total storage cost of the sR feature is 81639 bits. The paper says: "sR: Register | 6 x (2^7 + 2^8 + 2^9) x 8 | 6 x 65 x (2^3 + 2^3 + 2^3) | { valid (1), payload (14), decay_ctr (8) } x 65 | 53863" The correction did not land, so this field still says what it said -- resolve it before implementing. Also raised at /resource_accounting.
[/parameters/14] Under what exact condition is the register component's output suppressed (scaled by 0.0)?
[/state/7] The paper does not detail the exact layout or size of the inflight prediction metadata queue.
[/parameters/13] Is the multiplier value 2.5 robustly defined in the text beyond the figure label? Also raised at /parameters/14.

[/algorithms/1] The right-alignment at bit 3 is not definitively stated, and format classification for unrecognisable floats is unspecified. Since algorithms_1_variant_2 already exists, its range should be updated to address the format classification ambiguity. Also raised at /algorithms/1/pseudocode, /parameters/16/default.

[/algorithms/1] [source U3: Figure 6 (a) INT registers] the input marks this UNCERTAIN, so it must not be resolved by assumption: count encoding. Each count field is 6 bits, but a 64-bit register can have 0..64 leading (or trailing) identical bits, which needs 7 bits. The figure does not say whether the count saturates at 63, is taken modulo 64, or counts bits matching the sign bit (which caps at 63 naturally). The prose "the count of leading zeros (or ones)" also does not say how the zero/one case is distinguished - whether one extra bit encodes which, or whether the count is simply of bits equal to the MSB (resp. LSB). Also raised at /algorithms/1/pseudocode, /parameters/15/default, /unit_tests/1/expect, /parameters/17/default.

[source I15: Figure 6 (b) FP registers] the input marks this INFERRED -- a reading of the figure's layout that the paper never states -- so whatever the spec derives from it is an assumption and not a fact: semantics agree with the prose: in each IEEE-754 format the named slice is exactly the sign bit followed by the high-order exponent bits (8 of 11 for FP64, 5 of 8 for FP32, 2 of 5 for FP16).
How are ties resolved when multiple available registers in a bank share the same maximum usefulness score?
[/algorithms/1/pseudocode] How does the 6-bit count field encode counts up to 64 for integer registers?

[/algorithms/6/pseudocode] What is the exact boolean condition to determine if a bank was useful (for UT increment)? This is the same decision 'multiplier_not_useful' already carries; resolve it in that knob's range rather than as a second knob.
